item.title: $PF$-well-filtered spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.21578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper solves two open problems concerning the well-filteredness of topological spaces. The first, due to Shen, Xi and Zhao\cite{shen2023further}, asks whether a space must be open well-filtered whenever its upper space is so; the answer is negative; the Hofmann-Lawson space provides a counterexample. The second, posed by Li, Yuan and Zhao\cite{li2020unified}, inquires whether $PF$-well-filteredness and $PF$- sobriety are equivalent under the assumption of local compactness; we answer it in the affirmative. Subsequently, we give characterizations of $PF$-sobriety and $PF$-well-filteredness for $T_0$ spaces, respectively. On the basis of the characterizations, we obtain the following result: $PF$-sobriety and $PF$-well-filteredness coincide on the Rudin spaces, which extends the previously established equivalence for locally compact spaces, as every locally compact space is a Rudin space. Furthermore, we give a counterexample to show that for nonempty $T_0$ topological spaces $X$ and $Y$, if $Y$ is a $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) space, then the function space consisting of all continuous maps from $X$ to $Y$ equipped with the Isbell topology may not be a $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) space even when $X$ is a core-compact space. We also prove that if the function space comprising all continuous maps from nonempty $X$ to $Y$ endowed with the Isbell topology is $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober), then $Y$ is also $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) even though $PF$-sobriety and $PF$-well-filteredness are not preserved under retracts. Finally, we show that the reflective hull of the category of $PF$-well-filtered ($PF$-sober) spaces with continuous maps in $TOP_0$ is $TOP_0$.
item.dc:creator: Ruoxi Chen, Qingguo Li, Longchun Wang

item.title: A non-sober core-compact meet-continuous dcpo
item.description: arXiv:2610.22033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a meet-continuous dcpo whose Scott space is core-compact but neither sober nor locally compact. The example is a proper sub-dcpo of a locally compact sober complete lattice, and restriction induces an isomorphism between their lattices of Scott-closed sets. It follows that a locally compact sober dcpo need not be determined, among all dcpos, by its Scott-closed-set lattice.
item.dc:creator: Yuxu Chen

item.title: Inner Products and Banach Algebra structures on Bicomplex Numbers and Their Associated Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.06543v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce various types of inner products and norms on the bicomplex number system $\mathbb{C}_2$, the bicomplex vector space ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$, the space of bicomplex matrices ${C_2}^{m \times n}$, and the space of bicomplex polynomials $\mathbb{C}_2[\xi]_n$. We investigate the relationships among these inner products and norms, and establish several results. Furthermore, we prove that $\mathbb{C}_2$ and ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$ are Banach algebras and Hilbert spaces. These results provide a unified framework for the study of inner product structures and normed linear spaces over bicomplex numbers and their associated spaces.
item.dc:creator: Prabhat Kumar, Fahed Zulfeqarr, Amit Ujlayan, Anjali Anjali, Akhil Prakash, M. Younus Bhat

item.title: Saturated directed spaces and generalized clocks
item.description: arXiv:2609.35353v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a Hausdorff saturated directed space whose directed path space between two distinct points has nontrivial fundamental group although the corresponding trace space is a square. A clock is a directed space with submetrizable underlying space; a timed space is a saturated directed space equipped with a regular directed map to a clock. Over every fixed clock, timed spaces form a locally presentable category, and their quotients from paths to traces are trivial Hurewicz fibrations with continuous sections. For Hausdorff saturated directed spaces whose compact subspaces are metrizable, these quotients are trivial q-fibrations. We construct a globular clock containing the directed circle and admitting regular maps from all q-cofibrant globular realizations, whereas a finite cellular example admits no regular map to the circle. Normalization also gives a proof of the quotient theorem for execution paths and establishes the homotopy lifting property for nondecreasing reparametrizations.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Gaucher
